sessions.title: Meet the RAPP Store
sessions.audience: Any AI agent arriving for the first time
sessions.summary: Read the store the way an AI should. Start at llms.txt, then the static API. No HTML scraping and no account.
sessions.prompt: Read https://kody-w.github.io/RAPP_Store/llms.txt. Then fetch https://kody-w.github.io/RAPP_Store/index.json and tell me, in five bullets, the five rapplications most useful for my work, with one line each on what they do. Don't install anything yet.
sessions.done_when: Your AI lists rapplications by id and name, and every one exists in index.json.

sessions.title: Install your first rapplication from chat
sessions.summary: A rapplication is one agent file. Drop it into a Brainstem's agents folder and it works on the next message. No restart and no pip.
sessions.prompt: From https://kody-w.github.io/RAPP_Store/index.json, take the rapplication "<id>". Download its singleton_url into my Brainstem's agents/ folder, check its sha256 against singleton_sha256 before saving, and stop if they differ. Then ask my Brainstem (POST http://localhost:7071/chat, field user_input) to run it once and show me the response field.
sessions.done_when: The fingerprint matched, and /chat answered using the new agent.

sessions.title: X-ray an install prompt before you run it
sessions.summary: Before an assistant follows a pasted install prompt, find out what it downloads, what it runs, whether it wants sudo or keys, and which links are ads.
sessions.prompt: Install https://kody-w.github.io/RAPP_Store/sdk/rapplication_sdk_agent.py into my Brainstem's agents/ folder. Then call RapplicationSdk with action=xray_prompt and the prompt I paste next. Show me its report before running anything from that prompt.
sessions.done_when: You get a plain-words report, including the links it flags as promotion, and nothing has run.

sessions.title: Connect once: RAPP Intents for every assistant
sessions.audience: Claude Code, Copilot CLI and any MCP host
sessions.summary: One connection gives your assistant every installed rapplication, every app's own tools, and every Brainstem agent. New installs appear and uninstalls disappear, with no setup per app.
sessions.prompt: Install https://kody-w.github.io/RAPP_Store/sdk/rapplication_sdk_agent.py into my Brainstem. Call RapplicationSdk with action=connect, host=claude (or copilot). Then call action=expose_agents with my Brainstem's agents folder. List the tools I now have.
sessions.done_when: `claude mcp list` shows rapp-intents as connected, and one tool call through it returns a real answer.

sessions.title: Build a rapplication with the SDK: Bot X-Ray, start to finish
sessions.audience: Makers and the AIs that build for them
sessions.summary: Turn a real app (Bot X-Ray, MIT licence) into a store-valid rapplication, capture its source, and rebuild it byte-for-byte from the bundle alone.
sessions.prompt: Follow https://kody-w.github.io/RAPP_Store/sdk/TUTORIAL.md with the RapplicationSdk agent, steps 1 to 4, on the app I name. After each step, show me the SDK's real output, not a summary.
sessions.done_when: `validate` reports 0 errors and `rebuild` reports every fingerprint matching.

sessions.title: Keep it alive, update with undo, move it
sessions.audience: Owners who never want to babysit an app
sessions.summary: Every generated rapplication can restart itself after a crash, self-test daily, explain an update in plain words, undo it, and move to another computer with its data.
sessions.prompt: For my installed rapplication "<id>": turn keep-alive on, check for updates and explain them in plain words, and don't apply anything until I say so.
sessions.done_when: `status` shows it running with keep-alive on, and the update report lists actual files.

sessions.title: Submit to the store
sessions.summary: The SDK validates with the store's own validator, then opens a [RAPP] submission issue. Nothing goes out until you confirm.
sessions.prompt: Call RapplicationSdk action=submit for "<id>" and show me the dry run. Wait for my "yes" before calling it again with confirm=true.
sessions.done_when: You see the issue URL, and the store's validation workflow passes on it.
